chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding the old man and the old woman that they should both be flogged one hundred lashes;
and he ruled stoning for the married person (muhsan);

and he ruled regarding the virgin man and the virgin woman, when they commit fornication, flogging of one hundred lashes and exile for one year outside their own city — these are those who have had a marriage contract concluded but have not consummated it.

key_terms.أُمْلِكَا: Have been given in marriage — marriage contract (akad) concluded but not consummated
key_terms.الرَّجْم: Rajm — stoning; the prescribed punishment for a muhsan who commits zina
key_terms.الشَّيْخ/الشَّيْخَة: Old man/old woman — in jurisprudential context, refers to those who have had marital experience
key_terms.النَّفْي: Exile/banishment — secondary punishment for bikr fornicators alongside flogging
key_terms.الْبِكْر/الْبِكْرَة: Bikr — literally virgin; in fiqh, one who has not consummated a marriage
key_terms.الْمُحْصَن: Muhsan — married person; in fiqh, one who has had a valid, consummated marriage
key_terms.قَضَى: Ruled/judged — used throughout to introduce each judicial ruling of Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic hudud punishments for adultery and fornication according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) transmits the legal rulings of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishing three categories of persons subject to hadd punishment for zina (unlawful sexual intercourse): (1) elderly unmarried fornicators receive one hundred lashes; (2) married persons receive stoning (rajm); (3) unmarried persons (bikr) whose marriage contract has been concluded but not yet consummated receive one hundred lashes and one year's exile. This hadith is part of Muhammad ibn Qays's famous collection of Imam Ali's judicial decisions (qadaya), which is one of the earliest documented collections of Shia jurisprudence. The distinction between bikr (those who have contracted marriage but not consummated it) and muhsan (fully married persons) reflects a precise jurisprudential categorisation that shaped Shia fiqh on hudud penalties.
